before.en:
The Western Jin replaced Wei in 265 while Wu still ruled in the south. Reunification in 280 was one phase of the dynasty’s history, followed by renewed political fragmentation.

A Western Jin funerary urn in the Metropolitan Museum combines a model palace, auspicious animals and Buddhist figures. The museum interprets the combination as evidence of Buddhism entering existing beliefs about the afterlife. Political upheaval and changing religious practices belonged to the same world.
before.zh:
西晋于265年取代魏，南方的吴仍然存在。280年的统一只是王朝历史中的一个阶段，随后又出现政治分裂。

大都会博物馆的一件西晋魂瓶把楼阁、瑞兽与佛像组合在一起。馆方将这种组合解释为佛教进入既有来世信仰的证据。政治动荡与宗教生活的变化，发生在同一个历史世界中。

after.en:

A Western Jin funerary urn at the Metropolitan Museum (1992.165.21) raises a model palace above animals and rows of Buddhist figures. Its olive-green glaze covers a crowded, vertical miniature world. The museum interprets this combination as Buddhism entering existing beliefs about the afterlife.

大都会博物馆的一件西晋魂瓶（1992.165.21）在动物与成排佛像上方筑起楼阁模型。橄榄绿釉覆盖着密集向上延伸的微型世界。馆方将这种组合解释为佛教进入既有来世信仰的表现。

before.en:
The Eastern Jin maintained its court at Jiankang from 317 to 420 while competing states ruled in northern China. Liu Song later succeeded it at the southern capital.

Calligraphy, painting and ceramics developed amid these political divisions. A fourth-century green-glazed jar in the Metropolitan Museum offers a material example of southern production. Courtly culture and exchange continued across a landscape of competing regimes.
before.zh:
东晋于317至420年以建康为朝廷中心，北方则有多个政权并存。此后刘宋在南方都城继承东晋。

书法、绘画与陶瓷传统在政治分立中发展。大都会博物馆的一件四世纪青釉罐提供了南方制作的实物例证。朝廷文化与交流并未因政权竞争而停止。

after.en:
The Eastern Jin maintained its court at Jiankang from 317 to 420 while competing states ruled in northern China. Liu Song later succeeded it at the southern capital.

A fourth-century jar at the Metropolitan Museum (1977.449.8) gives the period’s ceramics a tangible scale: it stands just 7.3 centimetres high, with four lugs around its shoulder. The catalogue identifies Yue-type stoneware with green glaze.
after.zh:
东晋于317至420年以建康为朝廷中心，北方则有多个政权并存。此后刘宋在南方都城继承东晋。

大都会博物馆的一件四世纪罐（1977.449.8），为此期陶瓷提供可感的尺度：高仅7.3厘米，肩部有四系。馆方将其定为越窑式青釉炻器。

before.en:
Gaya comprised several polities in the southern peninsula rather than a single centralized kingdom. Their cemeteries shared forms of stone-lined chambers and pottery while retaining local differences. The combination allows archaeologists to investigate both connections and political autonomy. Burial similarities alone do not demonstrate one government.

Pottery and other specialized products circulated through regional relationships. Elite cemeteries occupied prominent positions near local centers, making authority visible in the landscape. Silla’s expansion brought the independent Gaya polities under its control by the middle of the sixth century. A confederated political history therefore sits beside the histories of larger kingdoms and challenges a map that fills all early Korea with only three uniform blocks.
before.zh:
伽耶由半岛南部的多个政体构成，并非单一中央集权王国。各地墓园共享石室结构与陶器形式，同时保留地方差异。考古学因此能够同时研究彼此联系和政治自主；葬俗相似本身不能证明存在统一政府。

陶器等专业产品通过区域关系流通。精英墓园常位于地方中心附近的显著位置，使权威在景观中可见。至六世纪中叶，新罗扩张逐渐结束了各伽耶政体的独立地位。这样的联盟型政治史应与较大王国并列，提醒我们不能只用三个整齐色块表现早期半岛历史。

A fifth-century long-necked jar in the Metropolitan Museum (1997.34.4) is attributed specifically to Great Gaya. Raised bands and textured strips divide its tall neck above a rounded body.
